newsitem.title: USA: Republican lawmaker attacks Fed's secretiveness.
newsitem.headline: Republican lawmaker attacks Fed's secretiveness.

text.p: The head of Congress's Joint Economic Committee on Tuesday criticized the Federal Reserve for being too secretive and said its closed-mouth policy was hindering his efforts to make price stability its sole goal.
"The Fed operates pretty much in a cloud of secrecy. It keeps policy mysterious," Rep. Jim Saxton told Reuters.

That secretiveness means that most lawmakers do not concentrate much on the central bank, the New Jersey Republican said, making it more difficult for him to win passage of his bill to change the Fed's mandate.

"It may take some time" for the bill to be passed, he said. A House Banking subcommittee is expected to hold hearings in due course on the measure. A Senate version of the bill was introduced by Florida Republican Sen. Connie Mack.

Saxton said that Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan would be open to changing the Fed's mandate to price stability, but that he would not want to be tied down to a specific target range. But without that, Saxton said, the bill would be "neutered."

"The American public deserves a wider window into the inner workings of the Fed, he said. Noting that virtually all hearings and deliberations in Congress are open to the public, Saxton said, "I'm not sure what makes the Fed different."
